reviewAdvisory: No supplied figure or evidence excerpt describes a 'filing' regime or a 'previous approval-based process', so this is an unsupported assertion about what the instrument replaced.
This attributes motive and historical context ('broader push', 'earlier crisis-response purchasing') that no supplied figure or evidence supports.

The two-or-one supplier figure supports that procurement may proceed with fewer bidders, but 'makes it easier for a single foreign supplier to win' is an inference not derivable from the supplied evidence.
The figures give the effective date but no article number; asserting 'Article 29' is a specific citation the draft cannot support from its supplied evidence.
The draft's own Inferred section concedes the 30% cap's calculation method is undefined, so listing it as flatly 'confirmed' is internally inconsistent.
Every substantive claim rests on one instrument and the draft never tells the reader it is single-sourced.
